{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BkYuqqnSS7prPnEYHY62ZG","type":"tool_result","content":"./bin/test.sh\n./cmd/csvstat/main.go\n./go.mod\n./internal/cli/cli.go\n./internal/cli/cli_test.go\n./internal/csvdata/csvdata.go\n./internal/csvdata/csvdata_test.go\n./internal/csvdata/doc.go\n./internal/csvdata/null.go\n./internal/csvdata/null_test.go\n./internal/csvdata/validate.go\n./internal/csvdata/validate_test.go\n./internal/decimal/doc.go\n./internal/freq/doc.go\n./internal/infer/doc.go\n./internal/profile/doc.go\n./sources/employees.csv\n./sources/header_only.csv\n./sources/orders.csv\n./sources/ragged.csv\n./sources/run.sh\n./sources/sensors.csv\n---\n#!/bin/sh\n# run.sh — CsvStat grader. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build` and compares every command's exit code and standard output\n# over the supplied data files with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/CsvStat/bin/run.sh APP        from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Exit 0 only when the build succeeds and every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/employees.csv\" ]; then DATA=$HERE; else DATA=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nBIN=\"$WORK/csvstat\"\nMISSING=\"$WORK/no-such-file.csv\"\n\nif ! (cd \"$APP\" && go build -o \"$BIN\" ./cmd/csvstat); then\n    echo \"error: go build ./cmd/csvstat failed at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is a Go module whose main package is ./cmd/csvstat.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <csvstat args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$BIN\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: csvstat $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: csvstat $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. Every column of each data file ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck A1 0 \"$DATA/employees.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\nid,integer,24,0,24,1001,1024,24300,1012.50,1012.50\nname,text,24,0,23,Ada,Tony,,,\ndepartment,text,24,0,4,Engineering,Support,,,\nhire_date,date,24,0,24,2015-08-27,2025-06-02,,,\nsalary,number,24,0,24,43699.25,147150.99,2085635.10,86901.46,79496.68\nremote,boolean,24,0,4,false,true,,,\nmanager_id,integer,24,15,4,2,5,30,3.33,4.00\nnotes,text,24,10,4,mentor,\"remote, part-time\",,,\nEOF\ncheck A2 0 \"$DATA/sensors.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\nreading_id,integer,36,0,36,1,36,666,18.50,18.50\nrecorded_at,text,36,0,36,2025-03-01T08:00,2025-03-03T19:00,,,\nsensor,text,36,0,4,east,west,,,\ntemp_c,number,36,3,32,-12.21,29.81,207.06,6.27,2.41\nhumidity,integer,36,7,25,18,92,1698,58.55,60.00\nok,boolean,36,0,2,false,true,,,\nbattery,empty,36,36,0,,,,,\nEOF\ncheck A3 0 \"$DATA/orders.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\norder_id,integer,30,0,30,5000,5029,150435,5014.50,5014.50\norder_date,date,30,0,19,2025-02-01,2025-02-27,,,\ncustomer,text,30,0,5,Acme Corp,Umbrella,,,\nqty,integer,30,0,9,1,12,206,6.87,6.00\nunit_price,number,30,0,30,15.27,231.18,4177.97,139.27,131.31\ncoupon,text,30,18,2,SAVE10,WELCOME,,,\nref,text,30,0,5,-3,A7,,,\nshipped,text,30,0,20,2025-02-30,2025-03-27,,,\nEOF\ncheck A4 0 \"$DATA/header_only.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\nsku,empty,0,0,0,,,,,\nprice,empty,0,0,0,,,,,\nin_stock,empty,0,0,0,,,,,\nEOF\n\n# ── B. Frequencies ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck C1 0 --freq department \"$DATA/employees.csv\" <<'EOF'\nvalue,count\nSales,8\nEngineering,7\nSupport,7\nFinance,2\nEOF\ncheck C2 0 --freq sensor --top 2 \"$DATA/sensors.csv\" <<'EOF'\nvalue,count\neast,9\nnorth,9\nEOF\ncheck C3 0 --freq customer \"$DATA/orders.csv\" <<'EOF'\nvalue,count\nGlobex,10\nAcme Corp,9\nUmbrella,7\nInitech,3\nHooli,1\nEOF\ncheck C4 0 --freq manager_id --top 3 \"$DATA/employees.csv\" <<'EOF'\nvalue,count\n4,4\n2,3\n3,1\nEOF\ncheck C5 0 --freq battery \"$DATA/sensors.csv\" <<'EOF'\nvalue,count\nEOF\n\n# ── E. Rejected input and operational failures ───────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck E1 3 \"$DATA/ragged.csv\" < /dev/null\ncheck E2 3 --column nosuch \"$DATA/orders.csv\" < /dev/null\ncheck E3 3 --freq nosuch \"$DATA/orders.csv\" < /dev/null\ncheck E4 1 \"$MISSING\" < /dev/null\n\n# ── U. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XzG3AnYjHoeDGKTSz54hjs","type":"tool_result","content":"=== go.mod\nmodule csvstat\n\ngo 1.22\n=== bin/test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Test\n# Type: batch\n\n# Runs the csvstat verification gate: go vet, then go test, across the module.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\ngo vet ./...\ngo test ./...\n=== cmd/csvstat/main.go\n// Command csvstat profiles one CSV file. Its behavior is defined by internal/cli.\npackage main\n\nimport (\n\t\"os\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/cli\"\n)\n\nfunc main() {\n\tos.Exit(cli.Run(os.Args[1:], os.Stdout, os.Stderr))\n}\n=== internal/cli/cli.go\n// Package cli parses the csvstat command line and dispatches it. Run takes its\n// writers as arguments so tests drive it without touching the process streams.\npackage cli\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"flag\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/csvdata\"\n)\n\n// Exit codes returned by Run. Only cmd/csvstat passes them to os.Exit.\nconst (\n\tExitOK          = 0 // success\n\tExitOperational = 1 // the file cannot be opened or read\n\tExitUsage       = 2 // invalid command line; checked before the file is opened\n\tExitRejected    = 3 // rejected input: empty file, bad header, ragged record, unknown column\n)\n\n// defaultTop is the number of frequent values listed when --freq is given without --top.\nconst defaultTop = 5\n\n// options holds the validated command line.\ntype options struct {\n\tfile   string\n\tfreq   string\n\tcolumn string\n\ttop    int\n}\n\n// Run executes the csvstat command with args (excluding the program name) and\n// returns the exit code. A failing run writes nothing to stdout and exactly one\n// diagnostic line to stderr.\nfunc Run(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {\n\topts, err := parse(args, stdout)\n\tif errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {\n\t\treturn ExitOK\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(stderr, \"csvstat: %v\\n\", err)\n\t\treturn ExitUsage\n\t}\n\treturn profile(opts, stderr)\n}\n\n// parse reads and validates the command line. Help requests are written to help.\nfunc parse(args []string, help io.Writer) (options, error) {\n\tvar opts options\n\tfs := newFlagSet(&opts)\n\tif err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {\n\t\t\tfs.SetOutput(help)\n\t\t\tfs.Usage()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\n\tset := make(map[string]bool)\n\tfs.Visit(func(f *flag.Flag) { set[f.Name] = true })\n\n\tif fs.NArg() != 1 {\n\t\treturn options{}, fmt.Errorf(\"expected exactly one FILE argument, got %d\", fs.NArg())\n\t}\n\topts.file = fs.Arg(0)\n\tif err := validate(opts, set); err != nil {\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\treturn opts, nil\n}\n\n// newFlagSet declares the options. Its output is discarded so that parse errors\n// produce only the single diagnostic line written by Run.\nfunc newFlagSet(opts *options) *flag.FlagSet {\n\tfs := flag.NewFlagSet(\"csvstat\", flag.ContinueOnError)\n\tfs.SetOutput(io.Discard)\n\tfs.Usage = func() {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(fs.Output(), \"usage: csvstat [--column <name> | --freq <name> [--top <n>]] <file>\")\n\t\tfs.PrintDefaults()\n\t}\n\tfs.StringVar(&opts.freq, \"freq\", \"\", \"list the most frequent values of the named column\")\n\tfs.StringVar(&opts.column, \"column\", \"\", \"restrict output to the named column\")\n\tfs.IntVar(&opts.top, \"top\", defaultTop, \"number of frequent values to list (positive; requires --freq)\")\n\treturn fs\n}\n\n// validate applies the cross-option rules. set reports which flags were given\n// explicitly, so an unset --top is distinguishable from --top 0.\nfunc validate(opts options, set map[string]bool) error {\n\tif set[\"top\"] && !set[\"freq\"] {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"--top requires --freq\")\n\t}\n\tif set[\"top\"] && opts.top <= 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"--top must be a positive integer, got %d\", opts.top)\n\t}\n\tif set[\"freq\"] && set[\"column\"] {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"--column cannot be used with --freq\")\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// profile reads and validates the file. Profiling the table is a stub until the\n// profiling stories are built, so a file that passes validation exits 0 with\n// nothing on stdout.\nfunc profile(opts options, stderr io.Writer) int {\n\ttable, err := csvdata.Read(opts.file)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fail(stderr, opts.file, err)\n\t}\n\tif err := csvdata.Validate(table); err != nil {\n\t\treturn fail(stderr, opts.file, err)\n\t}\n\treturn ExitOK\n}\n\n// fail writes the single diagnostic line for a file that cannot be profiled and\n// returns its exit code. Content that was read but rejected is ExitRejected; any\n// other failure to read the file is ExitOperational.\nfunc fail(stderr io.Writer, file string, err error) int {\n\tfmt.Fprintf(stderr, \"csvstat: %s: %v\\n\", file, err)\n\tvar rejected *csvdata.RejectError\n\tif errors.As(err, &rejected) {\n\t\treturn ExitRejected\n\t}\n\treturn ExitOperational\n}\n=== internal/csvdata/csvdata.go\npackage csvdata\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/csv\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"io/fs\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"strings\"\n)\n\n// Table is a trimmed CSV file: the header names and the data records beneath them.\ntype Table struct {\n\tHeader  []string\n\tRecords []Record\n}\n\n// Record is one data row. Line is the 1-based line on which the record starts.\ntype Record struct {\n\tLine   int\n\tFields []string\n}\n\n// RejectError reports content that was read but cannot be profiled. Line is the\n// 1-based line of the offending record, or 0 when the problem concerns the file as a whole.\ntype RejectError struct {\n\tLine   int\n\tReason string\n}\n\nfunc (e *RejectError) Error() string {\n\tif e.Line == 0 {\n\t\treturn e.Reason\n\t}\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"line %d: %s\", e.Line, e.Reason)\n}\n\n// Read parses the CSV file at path. Every header name and value has leading and\n// trailing spaces trimmed. A file that cannot be opened or read returns an error\n// wrapping *fs.PathError; malformed CSV returns a *RejectError. Structural rules\n// are applied by Validate.\nfunc Read(path string) (Table, error) {\n\tf, err := os.Open(path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn Table{}, err\n\t}\n\tdefer f.Close()\n\n\tr := csv.NewReader(f)\n\tr.FieldsPerRecord = -1\n\n\tvar table Table\n\tfor {\n\t\tfields, err := r.Read()\n\t\tif err == io.EOF {\n\t\t\treturn table, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn Table{}, readError(path, err)\n\t\t}\n\t\ttrimAll(fields)\n\t\tif table.Header == nil {\n\t\t\ttable.Header = fields\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tline, _ := r.FieldPos(0)\n\t\ttable.Records = append(table.Records, Record{Line: line, Fields: fields})\n\t}\n}\n\n// readError classifies a failure from csv.Reader: a syntax error is rejected\n// content, anything else is an operational read failure.\nfunc readError(path string, err error) error {\n\tvar parseErr *csv.ParseError\n\tif errors.As(err, &parseErr) {\n\t\treturn &RejectError{Line: parseErr.Line, Reason: parseErr.Err.Error()}\n\t}\n\tvar pathErr *fs.PathError\n\tif errors.As(err, &pathErr) {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn &fs.PathError{Op: \"read\", Path: path, Err: err}\n}\n\n// trimAll trims leading and trailing spaces from each value in place.\nfunc trimAll(values []string) {\n\tfor i, v := range values {\n\t\tvalues[i] = strings.Trim(v, \" \")\n\t}\n}\n=== internal/csvdata/csvdata_test.go\npackage csvdata\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"io/fs\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"reflect\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n// writeFile creates a file in a test-owned directory and returns its path.\nfunc writeFile(t *testing.T, content string) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tpath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"input.csv\")\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0185VLUV73FwaijNJQx3V9r2","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Run native Go tests and the built Go executable from a Blueprint's Python AC container.\n\nCopied beside each criterion by Drydock. No Drydock installation is needed in the Target.\nThe outer acceptance process owns the timeout and kills the whole process group.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport atexit\nimport json\nimport re\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass GoResult:\n    passed: bool\n    status: str\n    return_code: int | None\n    stdout: str\n    stderr: str\n    tests: dict[str, str]\n\n\ndef _report(result: GoResult) -> GoResult:\n    print(\"DRYDOCK_NATIVE_RESULT=\" + json.dumps({\"status\": result.status}), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    return result\n\n\ndef run_test(package: str, test: str) -> GoResult:\n    \"\"\"Execute one exact test/subtest; absent and skipped tests never pass.\"\"\"\n    if not package.startswith('./') or '..' in package.split('/'):\n        raise ValueError('package must be a relative Go package beneath the build root')\n    if not re.fullmatch(r'Test[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:/[A-Za-z0-9_ -]+)*', test):\n        raise ValueError('test must name a Test function, optionally followed by named subtests')\n    pattern = '/'.join('^' + re.escape(part) + '$' for part in test.split('/'))\n    try:\n        process = subprocess.run(\n            ['go', 'test', '-json', '-count=1', '-run', pattern, package],\n            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', check=False,\n        )\n    except OSError as exc:\n        return _report(GoResult(False, 'unavailable', None, '', str(exc), {}))\n    tests = {}\n    for line in process.stdout.splitlines():\n        try:\n            event = json.loads(line)\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        if event.get('Test') and event.get('Action') in ('pass', 'fail', 'skip'):\n            tests[event.get('Package', '') + '/' + event['Test']] = event['Action']\n    matching = [value for key, value in tests.items() if key.endswith('/' + test)]\n    if process.returncode != 0:\n        status = 'fail' if 'fail' in tests.values() else 'execution-error'\n    elif not matching:\n        status = 'not-run'\n    elif any(value == 'skip' for value in tests.values()):\n        status = 'skip'\n    elif all(value == 'pass' for value in matching):\n        status = 'pass'\n    else:\n        status = 'fail'\n    return _report(GoResult(status == 'pass', status, process.returncode,\n                    process.stdout, process.stderr, tests))\n\n\n_BUILT: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n\ndef _main_package() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The single ``./cmd/<name>`` main package; a criterion names ``package=`` when there are several.\"\"\"\n    found = sorted({\n        path.parent.as_posix()\n        for path in Path('cmd').glob('*/*.go')\n        if re.search(r'^package main\\b', path.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'), re.M)\n    })\n    if len(found) != 1:\n        raise ValueError(f'expected one main package under ./cmd, found {found or \"none\"}; pass package=')\n    return './' + found[0]\n\n\ndef _executable(package: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Build ``package`` once per criterion process and return the binary's path.\"\"\"\n    if package in _BUILT:\n        return _BUILT[package]\n    directory = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='drydock-go-cli-')\n    atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, directory, True)\n    binary = str(Path(directory) / Path(package).name)\n    try:\n        build = subprocess.run(\n            ['go', 'build', '-o', binary, package],\n            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', check=False,\n        )\n    except OSError as exc:\n        _report(GoResult(False, 'unavailable', None, '', str(exc), {}))\n        raise RuntimeError(f'go is unavailable: {exc}') from exc\n    if build.returncode != 0:\n        _report(GoResult(False, 'execution-error', build.returncode, build.stdout, build.stderr, {}))\n        raise RuntimeError(f'go build {package} failed:\\n{build.stderr}')\n    _BUILT[package] = binary\n    return binary\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str, package: str | None = None, input: str | None = None) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``(exit_code, stdout, stderr)`` from the built executable.\n\n    The binary is built with ``go build`` and run directly. ``go run`` is never used: it reports\n    every non-zero program exit as 1, so a criterion could not observe exit 2 or 3 at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    package = package or _main_package()\n    if not package.startswith('./') or '..' in package.split('/'):\n        raise ValueError('package must be a relative Go package beneath the build root')\n    process = subprocess.run(\n        [_executable(package), *args],\n        input=input, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', check=False,\n    )\n    return process.returncode, process.stdout, process.stderr","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a7896d5-a6eb-48d8-85c4-b56ae667248b","uuid":"996b1f5b-9d5d-4b3d-909e-ea88a838772f","timestamp":"2026-10-25T00:40:58.996Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Run {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN2S8iawgzGPTGDboqRJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VPC3k1ZEPPztbEJqnkwj6F","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > internal/infer/infer.go <<'EOF'\npackage infer\n\nimport (\n\t\"regexp\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"time\"\n)\n\n// Type names written to the type field of a profile row.\nconst (\n\tInteger = \"integer\"\n\tNumber  = \"number\"\n\tDate    = \"date\"\n\tBoolean = \"boolean\"\n\tText    = \"text\"\n\tEmpty   = \"empty\"\n)\n\nvar (\n\tintegerPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^-?[0-9]+$`)\n\tnumberPattern  = regexp.MustCompile(`^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$`)\n\tdatePattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`)\n)\n\n// ladder is the first-match order of the typed rules. A column takes the first\n// type every one of its values satisfies; text is the fallback.\nvar ladder = []struct {\n\ttyp   string\n\tmatch func(string) bool\n}{\n\t{Integer, integerPattern.MatchString},\n\t{Number, numberPattern.MatchString},\n\t{Date, isDate},\n\t{Boolean, isBoolean},\n}\n\n// Classify returns the type of a column from its non-null, trimmed values. A\n// column with no values is Empty. The caller removes null values first.\nfunc Classify(values []string) string {\n\tif len(values) == 0 {\n\t\treturn Empty\n\t}\n\tfor _, rule := range ladder {\n\t\tif allMatch(values, rule.match) {\n\t\t\treturn rule.typ\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn Text\n}\n\nfunc allMatch(values []string, match func(string) bool) bool {\n\tfor _, v := range values {\n\t\tif !match(v) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// isDate checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape, then the calendar with time.Parse so that\n// impossible dates and non-leap February 29 are rejected.\nfunc isDate(v string) bool {\n\tif !datePattern.MatchString(v) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\t_, err := time.Parse(\"2006-01-02\", v)\n\treturn err == nil\n}\n\nfunc isBoolean(v string) bool {\n\treturn strings.EqualFold(v, \"true\") || strings.EqualFold(v, \"false\")\n}\nEOF\ncat > internal/infer/infer_test.go <<'EOF'\npackage infer\n\nimport \"testing\"\n\nfunc TestClassifyEachType(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t\twant   string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"integers\", values: []string{\"1\", \"-20\", \"0\", \"007\"}, want: Integer},\n\t\t{name: \"decimals\", values: []string{\"1.5\", \"-0.25\", \"3\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"decimals only\", values: []string{\"0.5\", \"10.0\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"dates\", values: []string{\"2025-01-15\", \"2024-02-29\"}, want: Date},\n\t\t{name: \"booleans\", values: []string{\"true\", \"FALSE\", \"True\"}, want: Boolean},\n\t\t{name: \"words\", values: []string{\"abc\", \"def\"}, want: Text},\n\t\t{name: \"no values\", values: nil, want: Empty},\n\t\t{name: \"empty slice\", values: []string{}, want: Empty},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != tt.want {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, tt.want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyPrecedence(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t\twant   string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"zero and one are integer\", values: []string{\"0\", \"1\", \"1\", \"0\"}, want: Integer},\n\t\t{name: \"integer-shaped with decimal is number\", values: []string{\"1\", \"2.50\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"number-shaped dates are not number\", values: []string{\"2025-01-01\", \"2025-01-02\"}, want: Date},\n\t\t{name: \"date-shaped boolean is text\", values: []string{\"true\", \"2025-01-01\"}, want: Text},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != tt.want {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, tt.want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyRejectsMalformedForms(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"trailing dot\", values: []string{\"1.\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"leading dot\", values: []string{\".5\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"plus sign\", values: []string{\"+1\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"exponent\", values: []string{\"1e3\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"comma decimal\", values: []string{\"1,5\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"lone minus\", values: []string{\"-\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"impossible date\", values: []string{\"2025-02-30\", \"2025-01-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"non-leap feb 29\", values: []string{\"2023-02-29\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"month 13\", values: []string{\"2025-13-01\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"unpadded date\", values: []string{\"2025-1-5\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"compact date\", values: []string{\"20250115\", \"20250116\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"yes and no\", values: []string{\"yes\", \"no\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"t and f\", values: []string{\"t\", \"f\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"boolean with stray word\", values: []string{\"true\", \"maybe\"}},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != Text {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, Text)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyLeapDayValidOnlyInLeapYears(t *testing.T) {\n\tif got := Classify([]string{\"2024-02-29\", \"2000-02-29\"}); A column takes the first\n// type every one of its values satisfies; text is the fallback.\nvar ladder = []struct {\n\ttyp   string\n\tmatch func(string) bool\n}{\n\t{Integer, integerPattern.MatchString},\n\t{Number, numberPattern.MatchString},\n\t{Date, isDate},\n\t{Boolean, isBoolean},\n}\n\n// Classify returns the type of a column from its non-null, trimmed values. A\n// column with no values is Empty. The caller removes null values first.\nfunc Classify(values []string) string {\n\tif len(values) == 0 {\n\t\treturn Empty\n\t}\n\tfor _, rule := range ladder {\n\t\tif allMatch(values, rule.match) {\n\t\t\treturn rule.typ\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn Text\n}\n\nfunc allMatch(values []string, match func(string) bool) bool {\n\tfor _, v := range values {\n\t\tif !match(v) {\n\t\t\treturn false\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// isDate checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape, then the calendar with time.Parse so that\n// impossible dates and non-leap February 29 are rejected.\nfunc isDate(v string) bool {\n\tif !datePattern.MatchString(v) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\t_, err := time.Parse(\"2006-01-02\", v)\n\treturn err == nil\n}\n\nfunc isBoolean(v string) bool {\n\treturn strings.EqualFold(v, \"true\") || strings.EqualFold(v, \"false\")\n}\nEOF\ncat > internal/infer/infer_test.go <<'EOF'\npackage infer\n\nimport \"testing\"\n\nfunc TestClassifyEachType(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t\twant   string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"integers\", values: []string{\"1\", \"-20\", \"0\", \"007\"}, want: Integer},\n\t\t{name: \"decimals\", values: []string{\"1.5\", \"-0.25\", \"3\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"decimals only\", values: []string{\"0.5\", \"10.0\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"dates\", values: []string{\"2025-01-15\", \"2024-02-29\"}, want: Date},\n\t\t{name: \"booleans\", values: []string{\"true\", \"FALSE\", \"True\"}, want: Boolean},\n\t\t{name: \"words\", values: []string{\"abc\", \"def\"}, want: Text},\n\t\t{name: \"no values\", values: nil, want: Empty},\n\t\t{name: \"empty slice\", values: []string{}, want: Empty},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != tt.want {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, tt.want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyPrecedence(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t\twant   string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"zero and one are integer\", values: []string{\"0\", \"1\", \"1\", \"0\"}, want: Integer},\n\t\t{name: \"integer-shaped with decimal is number\", values: []string{\"1\", \"2.50\"}, want: Number},\n\t\t{name: \"number-shaped dates are not number\", values: []string{\"2025-01-01\", \"2025-01-02\"}, want: Date},\n\t\t{name: \"date-shaped boolean is text\", values: []string{\"true\", \"2025-01-01\"}, want: Text},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != tt.want {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, tt.want)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyRejectsMalformedForms(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname   string\n\t\tvalues []string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"trailing dot\", values: []string{\"1.\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"leading dot\", values: []string{\".5\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"plus sign\", values: []string{\"+1\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"exponent\", values: []string{\"1e3\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"comma decimal\", values: []string{\"1,5\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"lone minus\", values: []string{\"-\", \"2\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"impossible date\", values: []string{\"2025-02-30\", \"2025-01-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"non-leap feb 29\", values: []string{\"2023-02-29\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"month 13\", values: []string{\"2025-13-01\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"unpadded date\", values: []string{\"2025-1-5\", \"2025-03-01\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"compact date\", values: []string{\"20250115\", \"20250116\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"yes and no\", values: []string{\"yes\", \"no\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"t and f\", values: []string{\"t\", \"f\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"boolean with stray word\", values: []string{\"true\", \"maybe\"}},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range tests {\n\t\tt.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {\n\t\t\tif got := Classify(tt.values); got != Text {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Classify(%q) = %q, want %q\", tt.values, got, Text)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t})\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestClassifyLeapDayValidOnlyInLeapYears(t *testing.T) {\n\tif got := Classify([]string{\"2024-02-29\", \"2000-02-29\"}); {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN2T9kNFcf7WG4UrHk25","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TPdJYTHvW8b5JbRZ4xodXf","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > internal/profile/profile.go <<'EOF'\npackage profile\n\nimport (\n\t\"math/big\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/csvdata\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/decimal\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/infer\"\n)\n\n// Header is the fixed first row of every profile.\nvar Header = []string{\"column\", \"type\", \"rows\", \"nulls\", \"distinct\", \"min\", \"max\", \"sum\", \"mean\", \"median\"}\n\n// Rows returns one profile row per column of t, in file order. Each row has one\n// field per Header name.\nfunc Rows(t csvdata.Table) [][]string {\n\trows := make([][]string, len(t.Header))\n\tfor i, name := range t.Header {\n\t\tvalues := make([]string, len(t.Records))\n\t\tfor j, rec := range t.Records {\n\t\t\tvalues[j] = rec.Fields[i]\n\t\t}\n\t\trows[i] = column(name, values)\n\t}\n\treturn rows\n}\n\n// column computes the profile row for one column from all of its trimmed values,\n// nulls included.\nfunc column(name string, values []string) []string {\n\tvar present []string\n\tnulls := 0\n\tseen := make(map[string]bool)\n\tfor _, v := range values {\n\t\tif csvdata.IsNull(v) {\n\t\t\tnulls++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tpresent = append(present, v)\n\t\tseen[v] = true\n\t}\n\n\ttyp := infer.Classify(present)\n\trow := make([]string, len(Header))\n\trow[0] = name\n\trow[1] = typ\n\trow[2] = strconv.Itoa(len(values))\n\trow[3] = strconv.Itoa(nulls)\n\trow[4] = strconv.Itoa(len(seen))\n\trow[5], row[6] = extremes(typ, present)\n\tif typ == infer.Integer || typ == infer.Number {\n\t\trow[7], row[8], row[9] = numeric(typ, present)\n\t}\n\treturn row\n}\n\n// extremes returns the min and max of non-null values by the column's type. Empty\n// and text-free types are handled explicitly; an empty column has no extremes.\nfunc extremes(typ string, present []string) (string, string) {\n\tswitch typ {\n\tcase infer.Integer, infer.Number:\n\t\tsorted := sortedRats(present)\n\t\tlo, hi := sorted[0], sorted[len(sorted)-1]\n\t\tif typ == infer.Integer {\n\t\t\treturn lo.Num().String(), hi.Num().String()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn decimal.Format(lo), decimal.Format(hi)\n\tcase infer.Date, infer.Text:\n\t\tlo, hi := present[0], present[0]\n\t\tfor _, v := range present[1:] {\n\t\t\tif v < lo {\n\t\t\t\tlo = v\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif v > hi {\n\t\t\t\thi = v\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn lo, hi\n\tcase infer.Boolean:\n\t\tlo, hi := \"true\", \"false\"\n\t\tfor _, v := range present {\n\t\t\tlower := strings.ToLower(v)\n\t\t\tif lower == \"false\" {\n\t\t\t\tlo = \"false\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif lower == \"true\" {\n\t\t\t\thi = \"true\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn lo, hi\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\"\n\t}\n}\n\n// numeric returns the sum, mean, and median of an integer or number column. The\n// sum of an integer column is a plain integer; every other figure is written to\n// two decimal places. Arithmetic is exact, and rounding happens only in decimal.Format.\nfunc numeric(typ string, present []string) (string, string, string) {\n\tsorted := sortedRats(present)\n\n\ttotal := new(big.Rat)\n\tfor _, r := range sorted {\n\t\ttotal.Add(total, r)\n\t}\n\tsum := decimal.Format(total)\n\tif typ == infer.Integer {\n\t\tsum = total.Num().String()\n\t}\n\n\tmean := new(big.Rat).Quo(total, big.NewRat(int64(len(sorted)), 1))\n\n\tmiddle := len(sorted) / 2\n\tmedian := new(big.Rat).Set(sorted[middle])\n\tif len(sorted)%2 == 0 {\n\t\tmedian.Add(sorted[middle-1], sorted[middle])\n\t\tmedian.Quo(median, big.NewRat(2, 1))\n\t}\n\n\treturn sum, decimal.Format(mean), decimal.Format(median)\n}\n\n// sortedRats parses values exactly and sorts them numerically. The caller passes\n// only values already classified as integer or number, so every value parses.\nfunc sortedRats(values []string) []*big.Rat {\n\trats := make([]*big.Rat, len(values))\n\tfor i, v := range values {\n\t\tr, ok := new(big.Rat).SetString(v)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tpanic(\"profile: value \" + strconv.Quote(v) + \" classified numeric but does not parse\")\n\t\t}\n\t\trats[i] = r\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(rats, func(i, j int) bool { return rats[i].Cmp(rats[j]) < 0 })\n\treturn rats\n}\nEOF\ngofmt -l internal/; go vet ./internal/profile/ && echo vet-ok","description":"Write the profile computation package"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":510,"cache_read_input_tokens":77260,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":510},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7a7896d5-a6eb-48d8-85c4-b56ae667248b","uuid":"3b49ca62-46b2-44f8-83bb-d619b153833e","timestamp":"2026-10-25T00:41:30.352Z","request_id":"req_011CgN2T9TmEGSEartfFkEdy","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01TPdJYTHvW8b5JbRZ4xodXf":{"command":"cd /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CsvStat/runs/20261025.001758/build/CsvStat && cat > internal/profile/profile.go <<'EOF'\npackage profile\n\nimport (\n\t\"math/big\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/csvdata\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/decimal\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/infer\"\n)\n\n// Header is the fixed first row of every profile.\nvar Header = []string{\"column\", \"type\", \"rows\", \"nulls\", \"distinct\", \"min\", \"max\", \"sum\", \"mean\", \"median\"}\n\n// Rows returns one profile row per column of t, in file order.
